standard_prerequisites.name: Induction along a loop
standard_prerequisites.statement: To define a dependent function over the circle it suffices to give its value at the base point and the dependent path required when the point varies along the generating loop.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is how the self-homotopy is constructed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in the loop family
standard_prerequisites.statement: Transporting a loop along a loop in the family x is a path from x to x computes as the inverse of one loop concatenated with the other and with the first again.
standard_prerequisites.use: It turns the required dependent path into a concatenation identity.

standard_prerequisites.name: The generating loop is not trivial
standard_prerequisites.statement: The generating loop of the circle is not equal to the reflexivity path at the base point.
standard_prerequisites.use: It distinguishes the constructed self-homotopy from the reflexivity family, and it is retained as a navigation pointer.

core_obligations: Define a dependent function from the circle to its own path family by circle induction, assigning the generating loop at the base point (source lines 460-461).

Determine the dependent path required when the point varies along the generating loop and compute it as the statement that the inverse of the loop concatenated with the loop and with the loop again equals the loop (source lines 461-464).
Prove that concatenation identity by cancelling an inverse (source line 464).
Show the resulting self-homotopy differs from the reflexivity family by evaluating both at the base point, where the claim is exactly the non-triviality of the generating loop (source lines 466-467).

proof_roadmap.step: Construct the self-homotopy by circle induction and settle the loop case.
Evaluate at the base point to separate it from the reflexivity family.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 456-458 (book Theorem 6.4.2): there is an element of the family of self-paths of the circle which is not the family sending every point to reflexivity. The statement asserts an existence and a disequality, and the proof (source lines 459-468) builds the witness: it defines a dependent function by circle induction, which forces it to produce the dependent path required at the generating loop, computes that transport through the loop family as a concatenation identity, and discharges it by cancelling an inverse; the disequality is then obtained by evaluating both families at the base point, where it reduces to the previously established non-triviality of the generating loop. The transport computation at the path constructor is the substance and it is invisible in the statement.
